source_text:
Quid erat ergo iuxta illud latus terrae. quam inlustrem ac sanctam uocas? terra, inquit. tenebrarum. quid? de ista terra saltem concedis, quod corporea erat. necesse est te hoc dicere, quandoquidem omnia corpora inde adseris originem ducere. quid ergo ? quaeso. quamuis tardi, quamuis carnales homines, ne hoc quidem aliquando animadueritis. quod lateribus sibi iungi utraque ista terra non posset. nisi esset utraque corporea? cur ergo nobis dicebatur nescio qua caecitate peruersis tenebrarum tantum terram fuisse uel esse copoream, illam uero, quae terra luminis diceretur, incorpoream et spiritalem credi oportere? expergiscamur aliquando homines boni et saltem admoniti. quod facillimum est. adtendamus duas terras sibi lateribus non posse coniungi. nisi utrumque sit corpus.
Aut si ad ista etiam crassi et tardi sumus. quaero. utrum et ipsa terra tenebrarum unum latus habuerit et cetera infinita sicut terra lucis. non ita credunt; timent enim. ne deo uideatur aequalis. dicunt ergo illam per profundum inmensam . et per longum. sursum uersus autem supra illam spatia infinitae inanitatis adfirmant. et ne ipsa uel simplum, terra autem luminis duplum tenere uideatur, angustant eam a duobus etiam lateribus. tamquam si unus panis — sic enim, quod dicitur, facilius uideri potest — in quadras quattuor decussatim formetur. in quibus tres sint candidae, una nigra; modo de tribus candidis tolle distinctionem et fac illas et sursum uersus et deorsum uersus et undique retro infinitas: sic ab eis esse creditur terra lucis. illam uero nigram quadram fac deorsum uersus et retro infinitam. supra se autem inmensam inanitatem habere: sic opinantur esse terram tenebrarum. sed haec nimis adtentis et studiose inquirentibus quasi secreta demonstrant.
thought_title: Two lands joined at their sides must both be bodies
orientation: Augustine is quoting and then attacking Mani's description of the land of light and the land of darkness as two lands joined at one side.
pass_a_gloss: What therefore was beside that side of the land which you call bright and holy? The land, he says, of darkness. What? Do you at least concede about this land that it was corporeal? You are forced to say this, since you assert that all bodies take their origin from there. What then? I ask. However slow, however carnal men, have you not even this at some time noticed, that each of these two lands could not be joined to each other at their sides unless each was corporeal? Why therefore was it said to us, perverted by I know not what blindness, that only the land of darkness was or is corporeal, but that that land which is called the land of light ought to be believed incorporeal and spiritual? Let us wake up at some time, good men, and at least having been warned, which is very easy, let us attend to the fact that two lands cannot be joined to each other at their sides unless each is a body. Or if we are even thick and slow at these things, I ask whether the land of darkness itself also had one side and the rest infinite, like the land of light. They do not believe so; for they fear lest it seem equal to God. They say therefore that it is immense through depth and through length, but upward above it they affirm spaces of infinite emptiness. And lest it seem to hold even a single portion while the land of light holds a double portion, they narrow it from two sides also. As if one loaf — for thus, as is said, it can be seen more easily — were formed crosswise into four quarters, in which three are white, one black; now from the three white ones take away the distinction and make them infinite upward and downward and everywhere behind: thus the land of light is believed by them to be. But make that black quarter infinite downward and behind, but above itself to have immense emptiness: thus they think the land of darkness to be. But these things they show as if secrets to those who are very attentive and eagerly inquiring.

choices.why: Fixed glossary term for Mani's realm of evil.
Fixed glossary term for Mani's realm of God.
Augustine's key distinction: a land joined at sides must be bodily, not spiritual.
Renders the void Manichaeans posit above the land of darkness; 'emptiness' keeps the spatial sense.
The loaf analogy: 'decussatim' means in the form of an X, dividing into four parts.

pass_b_english: What, then, was next to the side of that land you call bright and holy? The land of darkness, Mani says. What? Do you at least admit that this land was corporeal? You have to say this, since you claim that all bodies take their origin from it. So I ask you: however slow, however carnal you are, have you never even noticed that these two lands could not be joined to each other at their sides unless both were corporeal? Why, then, were we told—through some perverse blindness, I do not know—that only the land of darkness was or is corporeal, while the one called the land of light must be believed to be incorporeal and spiritual? Let us wake up at last, good people, and, now that we have been reminded, at least notice what is very easy to see: two lands cannot be joined at their sides unless each is a body.

But if we are still too dense and slow even for this, I ask whether the land of darkness itself had one side and was infinite in all other directions, like the land of light. They do not believe that, for they are afraid it might seem equal to God. So they say it is immense in depth and in length, but above it they assert there are spaces of infinite emptiness. And so that it may not seem to occupy even a single share while the land of light occupies a double one, they narrow it on two sides as well. It is as if a single loaf—for what is being said can be seen more easily this way—were formed crosswise into four quarters, of which three are white and one is black. Now take away the division between the three white quarters and make them infinite upward and downward and everywhere backward: that is how they believe the land of light to be. Then make the one black quarter infinite downward and backward, but with immense emptiness above it: that is how they imagine the land of darkness. But they show these things as if they were secrets to the excessively attentive and those who inquire diligently.

problems.quote: But these things are shown as if they were secrets, and only to those who pay close attention and inquire diligently
problems.source_quote: sed haec nimis adtentis et studiose inquirentibus quasi secreta demonstrant
problems.why: "nimis" means "excessively/too much," not "close" attention. "nimis adtentis" = "those who are excessively attentive." The English loses Augustine's sarcasm about the absurdity being presented as esoteric knowledge.
problems.fix: But these things are shown as if they were secrets to those who are excessively attentive and inquire diligently

problems.quote: Let us wake up at last, good people, and at least take warning from what is easiest to see
problems.source_quote: expergiscamur aliquando homines boni et saltem admoniti. quod facillimum est. adtendamus
problems.why: Missing "admoniti" (having been warned/admonished). The Latin says "good people, at least having been admonished," not "take warning from."
problems.fix: Let us wake up at last, good people, at least admonished by what is easiest: let us attend
problems.ruling: 'admoniti' = 'having been admonished'; English 'take warning from' changes meaning and omits the participle.

edits.old: But these things are shown as if they were secrets, and only to those who pay close attention and inquire diligently.
edits.new: But these things are shown as if they were secrets to those who are excessively attentive and inquire diligently.

edits.old: Let us wake up at last, good people, and at least take warning from what is easiest to see: two lands cannot be joined at their sides unless each is a body.
edits.new: Let us wake up at last, good people, at least admonished by what is easiest to see: two lands cannot be joined at their sides unless each is a body.

fixed: Corrected 'close attention' to 'excessively attentive' to render 'nimis adtentis' accurately.
Restored the omitted 'admoniti' by changing 'take warning from' to 'admonished by'.

problems.source_quote: et sursum uersus et deorsum uersus et undique retro infinitas
problems.why: Latin has three directions: upward, downward, and backward everywhere; English merges into one phrase losing 'upward' and 'downward'
problems.fix: infinite upward and downward and everywhere backward
problems.ruling: Latin lists 'sursum,' 'deorsum,' 'undique retro' as distinct directions; English 'backward in every direction' loses upward and downward.

edits.old: make them infinite upward and downward and backward in every direction
edits.new: make them infinite upward and downward and everywhere backward

fixed: The English 'backward in every direction' merges the three Latin directions 'sursum uersus' (upward), 'deorsum uersus' (downward), and 'undique retro' (everywhere backward) into one phrase, losing 'upward' and 'downward'. Fixed to 'upward and downward and everywhere backward'.

problems.quote: But these things are shown as if they were secrets to those who are excessively attentive and inquire diligently
problems.source_quote: sed haec nimis adtentis et studiose inquirentibus quasi secreta demonstrant
problems.why: "nimis adtentis" = "to those who are excessively attentive," "studios inquirentibus" = "and to those who inquire diligently/zealously." But the Latin is ambiguous: are these the same people or two groups? The datives suggest "to the excessively attentive and to those who inquire diligently." The English merges them as one group. More critically, "demonstrant" = "they show/demonstrate"—active voice, not passive. The English "are shown" makes it passive, but the Latin says "they show these things as if secrets." The subject is presumably the Manichaean teachers/leaders. The English flips agency: "these things are shown" vs. "they show these things." This is a major agency error.
problems.fix: But they show these things as if they were secrets to the excessively attentive and those who inquire diligently
problems.ruling: 'demonstrant' is active 'they show,' not passive 'are shown.' Agency reversed: Manichaeans show secrets, not things shown to inquirers.

edits.old: But these things are shown as if they were secrets to those who are excessively attentive and inquire diligently.
edits.new: But they show these things as if they were secrets to the excessively attentive and those who inquire diligently.

fixed: Changed passive 'are shown' to active 'they show' to match 'demonstrant'; kept the two dative groups distinct as 'the excessively attentive and those who inquire diligently'.

fixed.quote: at least admonished by what is easiest to see
fixed.fix: and, now that we have been reminded, at least notice what is very easy to see
fixed.note: 'quod facillimum est' is an aside ('which is very easy') to 'adtendamus'; it is not what reminds us, and the English drops the verb 'let us notice'.

last_rejected.quote: through some perverse blindness, I do not know
last_rejected.source_quote: nobis dicebatur nescio qua caecitate peruersis
last_rejected.why: peruersis agrees with nobis: we were perverted by some unspecified blindness. English makes the blindness perverse and strands 'I do not know.'
last_rejected.fix: Why, then, were we, perverted by some blindness or other, told that only the land of darkness was or is corporeal
last_rejected.ruling: "nescio qua caecitate peruersis": 'by some blindness I know not what' is acceptable; English 'perverse blindness' keeps sense of perversis/caecitate; no meaning lost.

last_rejected.quote: And so that it may not seem to occupy even a single share while the land of light occupies a double one, they narrow it on two sides as well.
last_rejected.source_quote: et ne ipsa uel simplum, terra autem luminis duplum tenere uideatur, angustant eam a duobus etiam lateribus
last_rejected.why: Source: lest the land of darkness seem to hold only a single (share) and light a double. English garbles the logic: 'even' misplaced; the point is to avoid seeming to hold a mere single, not that darkness holds one.
last_rejected.fix: And so that the land of darkness may not seem to hold a mere single measure while the land of light holds a double, they limit it on two sides as well.
last_rejected.ruling: “vel simplum … duplum tenere videatur” means lest it seem to hold even one share while light holds a double; “even” correctly renders vel.
